flawed_step: Convergence in distribution only controls marginal distributions; it does not control the coupling between X_n and X needed for convergence in probability.
counterexample: Let Ω={0,1} with P({0})=P({1})=1/2. Define X(ω)=ω and X_n(ω)=1-ω for every n. Each X_n has exactly the same Bernoulli(1/2) distribution as X, so F_{X_n}(t)=F_X(t) for all t and hence X_n converges to X in distribution. But |X_n-X|=1 for every ω, so for ε=1/2, P(|X_n-X|>ε)=1 for every n. Thus X_n does not converge to X in probability.
assessment_summary: The statement is false, as shown by two identically distributed random variables that are oppositely coupled on the common probability space.
